html:
SMTO-SCH-0024 — The Agent's wait time didn't match what you asked

GUID: b21bd2a2-589b-4d8d-a964-4e17f6ac86a2
Slug: same-run-wait-timing-mismatch
Domain: SCH · Subsystem: sch

What happened

  • You asked the Agent to wait a certain time, but it tried to wait for a different length or until a different moment. SMTO stopped that wait and gave the Agent the correct time.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Keep the conversation open. The Agent normally retries the wait with the correct time on its own. SMTO hands the Agent the exact time from your message so it can fix the wait itself.
  2. If you meant a different wait, send a new message with the new time, for example "wait 30 minutes instead". SMTO only changes the wait when you say so, not when the Agent guesses.
  3. If the run stops, check whether the work already happened before asking for it again with the exact wait. This avoids doing the same work twice.

What success looks like

  • The run shows a wait that ends at the time you asked for, and the work starts after it.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't turn off the Enforce temporal routing check to get past this; it could make the Agent act at the wrong time.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Temporal routing rejected a same-run wait whose wake_at or delay_seconds differs from the captured timing, has the wrong numeric type, or combines wake_at with delay_seconds.

What this means

  • Same-run wait arguments differ from the captured absolute wake timestamp or relative delay, use the wrong numeric type, or combine wake_at and delay_seconds. Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.

Why this can happen

  • Same-run wait arguments differ from the captured absolute wake timestamp or relative delay, use the wrong numeric type, or combine wake_at and delay_seconds.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare exact expected wake/delay and exclusive field selection without silently changing timing.

How to fix it

  • temporal_routing.guard compares the proposed wait_for_event arguments with the captured same_run_wait: absolute waits must pass the exact expected_wake_at with no delay_seconds; relative waits must pass the exact numeric expected_delay_seconds with no wake_at. If the intended timing changed, obtain an explicit user clarification rather than altering the captured value.
  • Use the exact captured wake_at or delay_seconds, without combining both. Obtain a user clarification if the intended timing needs to change.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The accepted same-run wait uses the captured value or an explicit supported user amendment.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
